name: Right-Sided Heart Failure - Claims Optimized
remarks: Claims-optimized right-sided heart failure module
Enhanced ICU utilization and mortality modeling
All major billable activities occur within encounters
Improved BFD/CCW claim generation realism
Task 2.3 remediation (2026-08-10): Initial_Cardiology_Encounter used
to chain four `Medication_*_Supply_Delay` (30d each) + MedicationEnd
states BEFORE closing -- the banned Supply_Delay-while-open idiom,
holding the ambulatory encounter reservation for up to ~120 days
(4 lint CRITICALs + open-across). Fixed by ordering the four chronic
GDMT/PAH drugs (furosemide, lisinopril, sildenafil, bosentan)
back-to-back within the same visit, marking them chronic:true (the
engine's own annual renewal refills them -- no MedicationEnd),
and closing the encounter immediately after the last order.
Inpatient_Diuresis/ICU_IV_Diuresis/Ward_Diuresis had the identical
Supply_Delay idiom on IV furosemide -- never a legitimate 30-day
'supply' for a drug administered during a stay -- recoded as
administration:true injectable orders. Ward_Management previously
had no bounded length-of-stay at all; added one (Ward_Management_LOS,
matching the parallel Stepdown_Ward path's Ward_LOS). All CPT
Procedure codes recoded to SNOMED-CT (GMF codes must be SNOMED --
CPT is not in the export scanner's OK_SYSTEMS) with hcpcs_code_map
rows preserving the original CPT billing; Critical_Care_Billing
(CPT 99291) deleted rather than recoded as redundant E&M billing for
time the ICU encounter itself already covers. Six Observation states
(JVD_Observation + five *_BNP states) carried raw `"value": {...}`
blocks, an unrecognized GMF field silently dropped by Gson -- every
prior BNP/JVD record was NULL. Fixed: numeric BNP via top-level
`range` (LOINC 33762-6, unit pg/mL, already correct); qualitative
JVD via `value_code` (SNOMED 52101004, 'Present').
AUDIT CORRECTION (found during SMOKE, not in the fix spec):
CheckRiskFactors' risk-factor Guard checked two SNOMED codes
(13645005, 70995007) that no module in the tree ever assigns --
0% reachability at any population size, not a sampling artifact.
See CheckRiskFactors' own remark for the fix.
Task 5.4 remediation (2026-08-10/11): 'furosemide_40_mg_oral_tablet_rx'
and 'lisinopril_20_mg_oral_tablet_rx' were person-global attribute
names identical to ones written by heart/chf_meds.json (and its
nyha2/3/4 submodules), risking a future MedicationEnd/Guard in one
module silently acting on the other's order. Prefixed 'rshf_' here --
verified by grep that no other module reads the new names.
Task 2.3 AUDIT CORRECTION (found during SMOKE verification, not in
the original fix spec): this Guard checked SNOMED 13645005
('Chronic obstructive lung disease') and 70995007 ('Pulmonary
hypertension') -- neither code is ever assigned by ANY module in
this tree (grep-confirmed against the full modules/ directory).
copd.json diagnoses either 87433001 (Emphysema) or 185086009
(Chronic obstructive bronchitis), never the generic 13645005
umbrella concept. Pulmonary hypertension isn't diagnosed by any
module at all, under any code. Net effect: this Guard could NEVER
pass for any patient, at any population size -- not a small-sample
absence, a structural 0%-reachability defect that predates this
task (CheckRiskFactors was otherwise unchanged). Fixed by matching
the two codes copd.json actually emits; kept the pulmonary-
hypertension leg (harmless -- if some future module starts
diagnosing it, this Guard picks it up for free).
Task 2.3: dropped the raw ICD-10-CM code entry -- GMF codes must be
SNOMED-CT (export/condition_code_map.json already carries
10335000 -> the correct ICD-10-CM, confirmed present before this
change); ICD-10-CM is not in the scanner's OK_SYSTEMS set and was a
bad-system finding.
Task 2.3: a raw `"value": {...}` block is not a recognized GMF
field (Observation reads range/exact/value_code/etc, not `value`) --
Gson silently drops it and every prior record here was NULL. This
is a qualitative exam finding, so the fix is `value_code`, not a
numeric range.
Task 2.3: recoded from CPT 93306 (bad-system -- GMF codes must be
SNOMED-CT) to the standard transthoracic-echo concept, already used
for this exact clinical scenario in myocardial_infarction.json,
vhd_mitral.json, vhd_pulmonic.json, vhd_tricuspid.json, and the
tavr/savrr postop modules. export/hcpcs_code_map.json's existing
row for 433236007 only carried contrast-echo C-codes (C8923-C8930);
added a 93306 entry (unweighted, alongside the existing 5) so the
originally-billed CPT is actually reachable on export instead of
never appearing for any consumer of this SNOMED code.
Task 2.3: recoded from CPT 71046 to SNOMED 399208008, which
already carries the correct 71046 hcpcs_code_map row -- no map
change needed (same code pneumonia.json's ED_Chest_Xray uses).
Task 2.3: hoisted the raw `value` block into a top-level `range` (see JVD_Observation's remark for why the old form recorded NULL).
Task 2.3: this and the three preceding MedicationOrders used to
chain through named `Medication_*_Supply_Delay` (30d) + End states
BEFORE Initial_Encounter_End -- the banned Supply_Delay idiom, and
the reason this encounter held its lock for up to ~120 days
(lint CRITICAL x4 + open-across). All four are chronic GDMT/PAH
drugs (furosemide, lisinopril, sildenafil, bosentan) with no
clinical reason to stop at 30 days, so the fix is chronic:true +
same-visit ordering + immediate close, matching heart/chf_meds.json's
Task 1.7 pattern -- not a synthetic post-close delay chain, since
Maintenance_Loop already provides real next-visit cadence (30-90d)
immediately after this close.
Task 2.3: recoded from CPT 71045 to a distinct SNOMED concept from
the standard 2-view study (Chest_Xray's 399208008) so the portable/
mobile-unit CPT billing stays distinguishable; added the
hcpcs_code_map.json row (432769002 -> 71045).

remarks: Task 2.3: IV diuresis during an admission is a hospital
administration event, not a filled outpatient prescription -- a
30-day 'supply delay' was never correct for it (that was this
encounter's Supply_Delay-idiom CRITICAL). Recoded from the oral
313988 tablet to the injectable RxCUI 1719286 ('10 ML Furosemide
10 MG/ML Injection'), same code + administration:true idiom
congestive_heart_failure.json already uses for the identical drug;
its rxnorm_hcpcs_map.json row already exists (-> J1938), no map
change needed. administration:true rows don't stack, so no
assign_to_attribute/MedicationEnd (same idiom as pneumonia.json's
Task 1.5 inpatient antibiotics).
Task 2.3: this used to route through a separate Critical_Care_Billing
Procedure (CPT 99291, bad-system) before the ICU workup. Deleted
rather than recoded: a standalone 'critical care first hour' E&M
charge for time already covered by this same ICU encounter is
redundant billing for the same period, the same E&M-cleanup call
made for pneumonia.json's OutpatientManagement/FollowUpCare CPT
99213/99212 (Task 1.5) -- let the encounter itself carry the visit,
don't double-bill it with a separate procedure state.
Task 2.3: recoded from CPT 93503 to SNOMED; added the
hcpcs_code_map.json row (40403005 -> 93503).
Task 2.3: same IV-administration fix as Inpatient_Diuresis -- see its remark.

remarks: Task 2.3: new state. The death branch used to jump straight from
PostHospital_Mortality_Check to HF_Death while Stepdown_Ward was
still open (PostHospital_Mortality_Check runs before
Hospital_Discharge) -- Death is a valid closer per the lint tool's
own model, but the graph walk still flagged HF_Death as reachable
in both open and closed encounter contexts (it's also reached from
Maintenance_Loop/ICU_Mortality_Check/Recovery_Delay, all
post-close). Explicit close before Death here, same pattern Task
1.1 used for the CRPC death path.
Task 2.3: same IV-administration fix as Inpatient_Diuresis -- see its remark.
Task 2.3: new state. This direct-to-floor admission arm previously
had no bounded length-of-stay at all -- it went straight from the
(buggy) diuresis order into discharge. Gives it the same 2-5 day
LOS as the parallel ICU-stepdown path's Ward_LOS.
Isolated right-sided heart failure is uncommon; the risk-factor
Guard alone does not bound how many of those patients go on to
develop it.
Task 2.3: rate sourcing note (this state's probability itself is
unchanged -- out of this task's scope, which is encounter/coding
defects, not epidemiological calibration). Right-sided HF/cor
pulmonale in this population is overwhelmingly a late complication
of chronic hypoxemic lung disease or pulmonary arterial hypertension
progressing to RV pressure overload (MacNee W, 'Pathophysiology of
cor pulmonale in COPD', Am J Respir Crit Care Med 1994) -- the
Guard already requires COPD or pulmonary hypertension plus age
>=50. The 2% figure is retained as a deliberately conservative
first-pass placeholder pending dedicated epidemiological
calibration; no target share was specified for this module in the
Phase-2 fix spec.
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 4) -- the heart-failure
quartet. Four top-level modules each diagnose their own heart-failure code
with no coordination, so one patient could carry all four at once and run
four competing maintenance/decompensation loops against them:
congestive_heart_failure.json   88805009 Chronic congestive heart failure
high_output_heart_failure.json  10091002 High output heart failure
right_sided_heart_failure.json  10335000 Chronic right sided heart failure
valvular_heart_failure.json     42343007 Congestive heart failure
Rule: FIRST-TO-DIAGNOSE WINS. Each module tests the other three codes on its
own onset path; whichever module gets there first owns the patient's heart
failure and the other three stand down.
Only the primary code of each rival is tested. That is not a shortcut: the
record key is codes[0] (HealthRecord.conditionStart keys `present` by
primaryCode), so high_output_heart_failure.json's secondary ICD-10 entries
I50.9 / I50.89 never enter `present` and cannot be matched by an Active
Condition check. No module in the tree emits a ConditionEnd for any of these
four codes (verified by grep), so once one is set the other three modules'
checks stay true for life.
This is the EARLY gate. It sits before the cardiology encounter opens, so a
patient who already has a heart-failure diagnosis from a rival module never
gets this module's workup visit, its echo/BNP/imaging or its drug orders. No
encounter is open at this point, so Terminal leaks no encounter lock.
It is not sufficient on its own: State$Encounter.process returns false --
blocks across ticks -- while another module holds this person's encounter
lock, so the verdict here can go stale. The recheck below re-tests once the
encounter has actually opened.
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 4) -- the heart-failure
quartet. Four top-level modules each diagnose their own heart-failure code
with no coordination, so one patient could carry all four at once and run
four competing maintenance/decompensation loops against them:

high_output_heart_failure.json  10091002 High output heart failure
right_sided_heart_failure.json  10335000 Chronic right sided heart failure
valvular_heart_failure.json     42343007 Congestive heart failure

failure and the other three stand down.
Only the primary code of each rival is tested. That is not a shortcut: the

This is the LATE gate, and it is the one that makes the exclusion airtight.
It is the only predecessor of the ConditionOnset, that ConditionOnset has no
target_encounter (so it records its code the moment it processes), there is
no Delay or blocking state in between, and module processing is
single-threaded per person per tick. No rival can diagnose between this test
and this module's own diagnosis, in either ordering.
A hit here leaves the patient one cardiovascular-examination encounter with
no clinical content; it is closed explicitly rather than abandoned.
Closes the Initial_Cardiology_Encounter encounter when the cross-module heart-failure
recheck hands the patient to whichever module diagnosed first.
Required, not cosmetic: going to Terminal with the encounter still
open would hold this person's encounter lock for the rest of their
life -- the Class 6 defect the audit recorded against this very
module family (high_output_heart_failure.json).
